eligibility.evidence: Sec 1-3: ChatGPT and Llama 2 generate next utterances for SWDA and CHILDES excerpts; syntactic, lexical and semantic alignment (cites Garrod and Pickering 2004 alignment/priming) compared with human responses. Task is corpus continuation, so E2 (psycholinguistic paradigm by citation) is borderline.

A.title: Aligning to Adults Is Easy, Aligning to Children Is Hard: A Study of Linguistic Alignment in Dialogue Systems
A.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Human-Centered Large Language Modeling Workshop (HuCLLM, ACL)

paradigms.name: Linguistic alignment (syntactic, lexical, semantic) of a generated reply to an adult interlocutor, Switchboard excerpts
paradigms.source_paper: Garrod and Pickering 2004; Pickering and Ferreira 2008
paradigms.location: Sec 3.1-3.3, Table 3; Limitations notes corpora likely in training data

paradigms.name: Linguistic alignment of a generated parent reply to a child, CHILDES excerpts (24-42 months)
paradigms.source_paper: Misiek et al. 2020; Denby and Yurovsky 2019

D.population: adult English phone speakers (SWDA, 1157 transcripts); North American parents and children aged 24-42 months (CHILDES, 7721 transcripts); existing corpora, no new human data
D.metric: syntactic, lexical and semantic alignment (cosine) of true human responses

E.headline: ChatGPT aligns to adults at roughly human levels and Llama 2 above; both systems align below human levels when replying to children.

G.notes: Corpus continuation, not a cognitive experiment; alignment compared with raw human alignment, no tests or intervals, no baseline-adjusted effect. Labels follow ratio rule although authors state below-human (children). Temperature 0 vs 1 only in a footnote ('minimal effects'). Corpora likely in training data.
